prompts: Our new instrumentation shows conversations and turns in Weave's Agents view. I found the 'Set up custom monitors' guide, which talks about choosing operations on the Monitors page. We want a custom tag for answers needing human review. Can I follow that guide unchanged, or what setup should I use for these agent turns?

output.answer:
**Don't follow the "Set up custom monitors" guide unchanged. For agent turns, use a custom signal (a custom tag signal) instead.**

**Why**
- The custom monitors page calls monitors "the previous approach to monitoring production traffic." For new implementations, it says to use **Signals** under Weave for Agents [S2].
- The monitors steps are Calls-based. You open **Monitors** in the sidebar. Under **Calls to monitor**, you choose `@weave.op`s as **Operations**. The guide says an op only appears in that list after you've logged at least one trace that uses it [S5]. That is the legacy workflow, so don't mix it with the agent workflow.
- A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define. It then shows the result as a tag in the Agents view [S3]. That fits your "needs human review" tag.

**Setup for the tag** [S1]
1. In Forge, select your project. Then click **Agents** in the Weave project sidebar and open the **Signals** tab.
2. Click **+ Create your first signal** or **New signal**. Then click **Custom Signal**.
3. In the **Custom tags** drawer, set:
   - **Tag name**: for example, a label for answers needing review.
   - **Definition**: a prompt describing the behavior to detect. Weave sends it to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn. The judge applies the tag when the turn matches.
   - **Scorer name**: the name for the underlying scorer object.
   - **Inference model or custom runtime**: Serverless Inference is the default. It consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
4. Optional settings are under **Advanced**:
   - **Include tool calls** adds the turn's tool calls to the scoring context.
   - **Only score turns matching** filters by agent, operation, tool or model. Multiple filters combine with `AND`. If you leave it empty, every agent turn is scored.
   - **Sample rate** sets the fraction of matching turns that get scored. Lowering it can reduce cost on high-traffic agents.
5. Click **Create signal**. Weave then scores matching turns, and the tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab [S1].

**Caveats**
- The Signals page says the signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag. A tag signal might therefore run successfully even if you don't see any output [S4].
- The tag is applied by an LLM judge using your definition. I found no accuracy guarantee in the pages I read, so test your definition on real turns.

**Alternative:** if you'd rather decide with your own logic, a remote scorer signal sends each completed agent turn to an HTTP endpoint you host. It is used instead of an LLM judge, and the result shows as a tag or rating on the Signals tab. You can configure it with the Python SDK or the Weave UI [S6]. I read only the overview of that page.

**Next step:** create the custom tag signal with a narrow **Definition**. Optionally restrict it with **Only score turns matching**, then check the tagged turns in the Agents view.

# Set up custom monitors

> Passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues

> [!NOTE]
>
> Custom monitors are the previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page shows you how to set up custom monitors in Weave so you can passively score production traffic and surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. Use this guide when you want to define your own evaluation criteria, beyond Weave's preset signals, for production traces.

Monitors use LLM judges to passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. For example, you can monitor your application's responses for correctness or helpfulness, or you can monitor user input to identify trends in what users ask your agents about. Monitors automatically store all scoring results in Weave's database, so you can analyze historical trends and patterns.

You can monitor text, images, and audio in your application's input and output.

Monitors require no code changes to your application. Set them up using the Weights & Biases UI.

If you need to actively intervene in your application's behavior based on scores, use [guardrails](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/guardrails.md) instead.

To score calls with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md).

sources.heading: Create a monitor in Weave
sources.text:
## Create a monitor in Weave

To create a custom monitor in Weave:

1. Open the [Weights & Biases UI](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and then open your Weights & Biases project.

2. From the Weave sidebar, select **Monitors** and then select the **+ New Monitor** button. This opens the **Create new monitor** modal dialog.

3. In the **Create new monitor** menu, configure the following fields:
   * **Name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
   * **Description** (Optional): Explain what the monitor does.
   * **Active monitor** toggle: Turn the monitor on or off.
   * **Calls to monitor**:
     * **Operations**: Choose one or more `@weave.op`s to monitor. You must log at least one trace that uses the op before it appears in the list of available ops.
     * **Filter** (Optional): Narrow which calls are eligible (for example, by `max_tokens` or `top_p`).
     * **Sampling rate**: The percentage of calls to score (0% to 100%).
       > [!TIP]
       >
       > A lower sampling rate reduces costs, since each scoring call has an associated cost.
   * **LLM-as-a-judge configuration**:
     * **Scorer name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
     * **Score Audio**: Filters the available LLM models to display only audio-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Score Images**: Filters the available LLM models to display only image-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Judge model**: Select the model to score your ops. The menu contains commercial LLM models you have configured in your CoreWeave Forge account, as well as [Serverless Inference models](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless/models.md). Audio-enabled models have an **Audio Input** label beside their names. For the selected model, configure the following settings:
       * **Configuration name**: A name for this model configuration.
       * **System prompt**: Defines the judging model's role and persona, for example, "You are an impartial AI judge."
       * **Response format**: The format the judge uses to output its response, such as a `json_object` or plain `text`.
       * **Scoring prompt**: The evaluation task used to score your ops. You can reference [prompt variables](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/scorers.md#access-variables-from-your-ops-in-scoring-prompts) from your ops in your scoring prompts. For example, "Evaluate whether `{output}` is accurate based on `{ground_truth}`."
     * **Media Scoring JSON Paths**: Specify JSONPath expressions (RFC 9535) to extract media from your trace data. If you specify no paths, the monitor includes all scorable media from user messages. This field appears when you enable **Score Audio** or **Score Images**.

4. After you configure the monitor's fields, select **Create monitor**. This adds the monitor to your Weights & Biases project. When your code starts generating traces, you can review the scores in the **Traces** tab by selecting the monitor's name and reviewing the data in the resulting panel.

You can also [compare](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tools/comparison.md) and visualize the monitor's trace data in the Weights & Biases UI, or download it in formats such as CSV and JSON using the download button () in the **Traces** tab.

Weave automatically stores all scorer results in the [Call](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md#calls) object's `feedback` field.

> [!TIP]
>
> **This workflow is also available in CoreWeave Agent Lens.** Agent Lens is the Forge experience built for tracing, monitoring, and analyzing AI agents, with automated insights into agent failures and user intents. > [See how to do this in Agent Lens](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/agent-lens/tags/create-tag.md).

A custom signal scores agent turns against a behavior you define, then shows that result as a tag in the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-activity.md). When those built-in signals don't cover what you want to monitor, create a custom signal. This page shows you how to create that custom tag signal in the Weights & Biases UI.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

# Set up custom monitors

> Passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues

> [!NOTE]
>
> Custom monitors are the previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page shows you how to set up custom monitors in Weave so you can passively score production traffic and surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. Use this guide when you want to define your own evaluation criteria, beyond Weave's preset signals, for production traces.

Monitors use LLM judges to passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. For example, you can monitor your application's responses for correctness or helpfulness, or you can monitor user input to identify trends in what users ask your agents about. Monitors automatically store all scoring results in Weave's database, so you can analyze historical trends and patterns.

You can monitor text, images, and audio in your application's input and output.

Monitors require no code changes to your application. Set them up using the Weights & Biases UI.

If you need to actively intervene in your application's behavior based on scores, use [guardrails](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/guardrails.md) instead.

To score calls with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md).

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

## Create a monitor in Weave

To create a custom monitor in Weave:

1. Open the [Weights & Biases UI](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and then open your Weights & Biases project.

2. From the Weave sidebar, select **Monitors** and then select the **+ New Monitor** button. This opens the **Create new monitor** modal dialog.

3. In the **Create new monitor** menu, configure the following fields:
   * **Name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
   * **Description** (Optional): Explain what the monitor does.
   * **Active monitor** toggle: Turn the monitor on or off.
   * **Calls to monitor**:
     * **Operations**: Choose one or more `@weave.op`s to monitor. You must log at least one trace that uses the op before it appears in the list of available ops.
     * **Filter** (Optional): Narrow which calls are eligible (for example, by `max_tokens` or `top_p`).
     * **Sampling rate**: The percentage of calls to score (0% to 100%).
       > [!TIP]
       >
       > A lower sampling rate reduces costs, since each scoring call has an associated cost.
   * **LLM-as-a-judge configuration**:
     * **Scorer name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
     * **Score Audio**: Filters the available LLM models to display only audio-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Score Images**: Filters the available LLM models to display only image-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Judge model**: Select the model to score your ops. The menu contains commercial LLM models you have configured in your CoreWeave Forge account, as well as [Serverless Inference models](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless/models.md). Audio-enabled models have an **Audio Input** label beside their names. For the selected model, configure the following settings:
       * **Configuration name**: A name for this model configuration.
       * **System prompt**: Defines the judging model's role and persona, for example, "You are an impartial AI judge."
       * **Response format**: The format the judge uses to output its response, such as a `json_object` or plain `text`.
       * **Scoring prompt**: The evaluation task used to score your ops. You can reference [prompt variables](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/scorers.md#access-variables-from-your-ops-in-scoring-prompts) from your ops in your scoring prompts. For example, "Evaluate whether `{output}` is accurate based on `{ground_truth}`."
     * **Media Scoring JSON Paths**: Specify JSONPath expressions (RFC 9535) to extract media from your trace data. If you specify no paths, the monitor includes all scorable media from user messages. This field appears when you enable **Score Audio** or **Score Images**.

4. After you configure the monitor's fields, select **Create monitor**. This adds the monitor to your Weights & Biases project. When your code starts generating traces, you can review the scores in the **Traces** tab by selecting the monitor's name and reviewing the data in the resulting panel.

You can also [compare](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tools/comparison.md) and visualize the monitor's trace data in the Weights & Biases UI, or download it in formats such as CSV and JSON using the download button () in the **Traces** tab.

Weave automatically stores all scorer results in the [Call](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md#calls) object's `feedback` field.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

## Signals and custom monitors

Use [signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/monitors.md), preset automated scorers for production traces, to get started with production monitoring quickly, then add custom monitors for evaluation criteria specific to your application.

| | Signals | Custom monitors |
| - | - | - |
| **Configuration** | One-click enable, no prompt writing | Full control over scoring prompt, model, and parameters |
| **Scope** | Preset quality and error classifiers | Any evaluation criteria you define |
| **Trace selection** | Automatic (successful root traces for quality, failed traces for errors) | Configurable operations, filters, and sampling rate |
| **Model** | Serverless Inference (preset) | Any commercial or Serverless Inference model |
| **Use case** | Quick production monitoring with proven classifiers | Custom evaluation criteria specific to your application |

## Create a monitor in Weave

To create a custom monitor in Weave:

1. Open the [Weights & Biases UI](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and then open your Weights & Biases project.

2. From the Weave sidebar, select **Monitors** and then select the **+ New Monitor** button. This opens the **Create new monitor** modal dialog.

3. In the **Create new monitor** menu, configure the following fields:
   * **Name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
   * **Description** (Optional): Explain what the monitor does.
   * **Active monitor** toggle: Turn the monitor on or off.
   * **Calls to monitor**:
     * **Operations**: Choose one or more `@weave.op`s to monitor. You must log at least one trace that uses the op before it appears in the list of available ops.
     * **Filter** (Optional): Narrow which calls are eligible (for example, by `max_tokens` or `top_p`).
     * **Sampling rate**: The percentage of calls to score (0% to 100%).
       > [!TIP]
       >
       > A lower sampling rate reduces costs, since each scoring call has an associated cost.
   * **LLM-as-a-judge configuration**:
     * **Scorer name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
     * **Score Audio**: Filters the available LLM models to display only audio-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Score Images**: Filters the available LLM models to display only image-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Judge model**: Select the model to score your ops. The menu contains commercial LLM models you have configured in your CoreWeave Forge account, as well as [Serverless Inference models](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless/models.md). Audio-enabled models have an **Audio Input** label beside their names. For the selected model, configure the following settings:
       * **Configuration name**: A name for this model configuration.
       * **System prompt**: Defines the judging model's role and persona, for example, "You are an impartial AI judge."
       * **Response format**: The format the judge uses to output its response, such as a `json_object` or plain `text`.
       * **Scoring prompt**: The evaluation task used to score your ops. You can reference [prompt variables](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/scorers.md#access-variables-from-your-ops-in-scoring-prompts) from your ops in your scoring prompts. For example, "Evaluate whether `{output}` is accurate based on `{ground_truth}`."
     * **Media Scoring JSON Paths**: Specify JSONPath expressions (RFC 9535) to extract media from your trace data. If you specify no paths, the monitor includes all scorable media from user messages. This field appears when you enable **Score Audio** or **Score Images**.

4. After you configure the monitor's fields, select **Create monitor**. This adds the monitor to your Weights & Biases project. When your code starts generating traces, you can review the scores in the **Traces** tab by selecting the monitor's name and reviewing the data in the resulting panel.

You can also [compare](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tools/comparison.md) and visualize the monitor's trace data in the Weights & Biases UI, or download it in formats such as CSV and JSON using the download button () in the **Traces** tab.

Weave automatically stores all scorer results in the [Call](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md#calls) object's `feedback` field.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

# Set up custom monitors

> Passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues

> [!NOTE]
>
> Custom monitors are the previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page shows you how to set up custom monitors in Weave so you can passively score production traffic and surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. Use this guide when you want to define your own evaluation criteria, beyond Weave's preset signals, for production traces.

Monitors use LLM judges to passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. For example, you can monitor your application's responses for correctness or helpfulness, or you can monitor user input to identify trends in what users ask your agents about. Monitors automatically store all scoring results in Weave's database, so you can analyze historical trends and patterns.

You can monitor text, images, and audio in your application's input and output.

Monitors require no code changes to your application. Set them up using the Weights & Biases UI.

If you need to actively intervene in your application's behavior based on scores, use [guardrails](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/guardrails.md) instead.

To score calls with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md).

sources.text:
## Create a monitor in Weave

To create a custom monitor in Weave:

1. Open the [Weights & Biases UI](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and then open your Weights & Biases project.

2. From the Weave sidebar, select **Monitors** and then select the **+ New Monitor** button. This opens the **Create new monitor** modal dialog.

3. In the **Create new monitor** menu, configure the following fields:
   * **Name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
   * **Description** (Optional): Explain what the monitor does.
   * **Active monitor** toggle: Turn the monitor on or off.
   * **Calls to monitor**:
     * **Operations**: Choose one or more `@weave.op`s to monitor. You must log at least one trace that uses the op before it appears in the list of available ops.
     * **Filter** (Optional): Narrow which calls are eligible (for example, by `max_tokens` or `top_p`).
     * **Sampling rate**: The percentage of calls to score (0% to 100%).
       > [!TIP]
       >
       > A lower sampling rate reduces costs, since each scoring call has an associated cost.
   * **LLM-as-a-judge configuration**:
     * **Scorer name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
     * **Score Audio**: Filters the available LLM models to display only audio-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Score Images**: Filters the available LLM models to display only image-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Judge model**: Select the model to score your ops. The menu contains commercial LLM models you have configured in your CoreWeave Forge account, as well as [Serverless Inference models](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless/models.md). Audio-enabled models have an **Audio Input** label beside their names. For the selected model, configure the following settings:
       * **Configuration name**: A name for this model configuration.
       * **System prompt**: Defines the judging model's role and persona, for example, "You are an impartial AI judge."
       * **Response format**: The format the judge uses to output its response, such as a `json_object` or plain `text`.
       * **Scoring prompt**: The evaluation task used to score your ops. You can reference [prompt variables](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/scorers.md#access-variables-from-your-ops-in-scoring-prompts) from your ops in your scoring prompts. For example, "Evaluate whether `{output}` is accurate based on `{ground_truth}`."
     * **Media Scoring JSON Paths**: Specify JSONPath expressions (RFC 9535) to extract media from your trace data. If you specify no paths, the monitor includes all scorable media from user messages. This field appears when you enable **Score Audio** or **Score Images**.

4. After you configure the monitor's fields, select **Create monitor**. This adds the monitor to your Weights & Biases project. When your code starts generating traces, you can review the scores in the **Traces** tab by selecting the monitor's name and reviewing the data in the resulting panel.

You can also [compare](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tools/comparison.md) and visualize the monitor's trace data in the Weights & Biases UI, or download it in formats such as CSV and JSON using the download button () in the **Traces** tab.

Weave automatically stores all scorer results in the [Call](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md#calls) object's `feedback` field.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

# Set up custom monitors

> Passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues

> [!NOTE]
>
> Custom monitors are the previous approach to monitoring production traffic. For new implementations, use **Signals** under Weave for Agents. See [View agent signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page shows you how to set up custom monitors in Weave so you can passively score production traffic and surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. Use this guide when you want to define your own evaluation criteria, beyond Weave's preset signals, for production traces.

Monitors use LLM judges to passively score production traffic to surface trends and issues in your LLM applications. For example, you can monitor your application's responses for correctness or helpfulness, or you can monitor user input to identify trends in what users ask your agents about. Monitors automatically store all scoring results in Weave's database, so you can analyze historical trends and patterns.

You can monitor text, images, and audio in your application's input and output.

Monitors require no code changes to your application. Set them up using the Weights & Biases UI.

If you need to actively intervene in your application's behavior based on scores, use [guardrails](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/guardrails.md) instead.

To score calls with an HTTP endpoint that you host instead of an LLM judge, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md).

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

all_read_evidence.text:
## Create a monitor in Weave

To create a custom monitor in Weave:

1. Open the [Weights & Biases UI](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and then open your Weights & Biases project.

2. From the Weave sidebar, select **Monitors** and then select the **+ New Monitor** button. This opens the **Create new monitor** modal dialog.

3. In the **Create new monitor** menu, configure the following fields:
   * **Name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
   * **Description** (Optional): Explain what the monitor does.
   * **Active monitor** toggle: Turn the monitor on or off.
   * **Calls to monitor**:
     * **Operations**: Choose one or more `@weave.op`s to monitor. You must log at least one trace that uses the op before it appears in the list of available ops.
     * **Filter** (Optional): Narrow which calls are eligible (for example, by `max_tokens` or `top_p`).
     * **Sampling rate**: The percentage of calls to score (0% to 100%).
       > [!TIP]
       >
       > A lower sampling rate reduces costs, since each scoring call has an associated cost.
   * **LLM-as-a-judge configuration**:
     * **Scorer name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
     * **Score Audio**: Filters the available LLM models to display only audio-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Score Images**: Filters the available LLM models to display only image-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Judge model**: Select the model to score your ops. The menu contains commercial LLM models you have configured in your CoreWeave Forge account, as well as [Serverless Inference models](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless/models.md). Audio-enabled models have an **Audio Input** label beside their names. For the selected model, configure the following settings:
       * **Configuration name**: A name for this model configuration.
       * **System prompt**: Defines the judging model's role and persona, for example, "You are an impartial AI judge."
       * **Response format**: The format the judge uses to output its response, such as a `json_object` or plain `text`.
       * **Scoring prompt**: The evaluation task used to score your ops. You can reference [prompt variables](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/scorers.md#access-variables-from-your-ops-in-scoring-prompts) from your ops in your scoring prompts. For example, "Evaluate whether `{output}` is accurate based on `{ground_truth}`."
     * **Media Scoring JSON Paths**: Specify JSONPath expressions (RFC 9535) to extract media from your trace data. If you specify no paths, the monitor includes all scorable media from user messages. This field appears when you enable **Score Audio** or **Score Images**.

4. After you configure the monitor's fields, select **Create monitor**. This adds the monitor to your Weights & Biases project. When your code starts generating traces, you can review the scores in the **Traces** tab by selecting the monitor's name and reviewing the data in the resulting panel.

You can also [compare](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tools/comparison.md) and visualize the monitor's trace data in the Weights & Biases UI, or download it in formats such as CSV and JSON using the download button () in the **Traces** tab.

Weave automatically stores all scorer results in the [Call](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md#calls) object's `feedback` field.

# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.

## Signals and custom monitors

Use [signals](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/monitors.md), preset automated scorers for production traces, to get started with production monitoring quickly, then add custom monitors for evaluation criteria specific to your application.

## Create a custom tag signal

To create a custom tag signal:

1. Navigate to [Forge](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and select your project.

2. In the **Weave project sidebar**, click **Agents**.

3. In the tab bar, click **Signals**.

4. On the Signals tab, click **+ Create your first signal**, or **New signal**.

5. In the drawer, click **Custom Signal**.

   ![The Custom tags drawer with Tag name, Definition, Scorer name, and Inference model fields for creating a custom signal.](https://mintcdn.com/coreweave-dbfa0e8d/3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx/products/wandb/weave/_media/custom-signal.png?fit=max\&auto=format\&n=3Dv_sw2eg8feUJlx\&q=85\&s=b01a4b83a0ef2c7717d78efc406a1de0)

6. In the **Custom tags** drawer, configure the following fields:
   * **Tag name**: The label that appears in the Agents view for the behavior you want to monitor.
   * **Definition**: A prompt that describes the behavior you want the signal to detect. Weave sends this prompt to an LLM judge, which scores each agent turn and applies the tag when the turn matches the behavior. For example, to catch a specific product failure: "The user is discussing errors or issues regarding Product X."
   * **+ Add tag** (Optional): Click to define another tag on the same signal. For example, if you support multiple products, add a separate tag for each product so you can track frustration per product instead of only in aggregate.
   * **Scorer name**: The name for the underlying scorer object.
   * **Inference model or custom runtime**: The model used to score matching turns. [Serverless Inference](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless.md) is the default. CoreWeave Serverless Inference consumes credits from your CoreWeave Forge account.
   * **Include tool calls** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then check the box to include the turn's tool calls in the context sent to the scoring model.
   * **Only score turns matching** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then add one or more filters to restrict which turns the signal scores, for example by agent, operation, tool, or model. Leave empty to score every agent turn. Weave combines multiple filters with `AND` logic.
   * **Sample rate** (Optional): Expand **Advanced**, then set the fraction of matching agent turns the signal scores. For high-traffic agents, lower the sample rate to score a fraction of matching turns instead of every turn and reduce cost.

7. In the **Custom tags** drawer, click **Create signal**.

After you create the signal, Weave scores matching turns. The tag appears in the Agents view, including on the Signals tab.

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

## Create a monitor in Weave

To create a custom monitor in Weave:

1. Open the [Weights & Biases UI](https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb) and then open your Weights & Biases project.

2. From the Weave sidebar, select **Monitors** and then select the **+ New Monitor** button. This opens the **Create new monitor** modal dialog.

3. In the **Create new monitor** menu, configure the following fields:
   * **Name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
   * **Description** (Optional): Explain what the monitor does.
   * **Active monitor** toggle: Turn the monitor on or off.
   * **Calls to monitor**:
     * **Operations**: Choose one or more `@weave.op`s to monitor. You must log at least one trace that uses the op before it appears in the list of available ops.
     * **Filter** (Optional): Narrow which calls are eligible (for example, by `max_tokens` or `top_p`).
     * **Sampling rate**: The percentage of calls to score (0% to 100%).
       > [!TIP]
       >
       > A lower sampling rate reduces costs, since each scoring call has an associated cost.
   * **LLM-as-a-judge configuration**:
     * **Scorer name**: Must start with a letter or number. Can contain letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores.
     * **Score Audio**: Filters the available LLM models to display only audio-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Score Images**: Filters the available LLM models to display only image-enabled models, and opens the **Media Scoring JSON Paths** field.
     * **Judge model**: Select the model to score your ops. The menu contains commercial LLM models you have configured in your CoreWeave Forge account, as well as [Serverless Inference models](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/inference/serverless/models.md). Audio-enabled models have an **Audio Input** label beside their names. For the selected model, configure the following settings:
       * **Configuration name**: A name for this model configuration.
       * **System prompt**: Defines the judging model's role and persona, for example, "You are an impartial AI judge."
       * **Response format**: The format the judge uses to output its response, such as a `json_object` or plain `text`.
       * **Scoring prompt**: The evaluation task used to score your ops. You can reference [prompt variables](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/scorers.md#access-variables-from-your-ops-in-scoring-prompts) from your ops in your scoring prompts. For example, "Evaluate whether `{output}` is accurate based on `{ground_truth}`."
     * **Media Scoring JSON Paths**: Specify JSONPath expressions (RFC 9535) to extract media from your trace data. If you specify no paths, the monitor includes all scorable media from user messages. This field appears when you enable **Score Audio** or **Score Images**.

4. After you configure the monitor's fields, select **Create monitor**. This adds the monitor to your Weights & Biases project. When your code starts generating traces, you can review the scores in the **Traces** tab by selecting the monitor's name and reviewing the data in the resulting panel.

You can also [compare](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tools/comparison.md) and visualize the monitor's trace data in the Weights & Biases UI, or download it in formats such as CSV and JSON using the download button () in the **Traces** tab.

Weave automatically stores all scorer results in the [Call](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/tracing.md#calls) object's `feedback` field.

result.text:
# Score agent turns with a remote scorer

> Score Weave agent turns with your own HTTP endpoint and see the results as tags or ratings on the Signals tab.

A remote scorer signal scores each completed agent turn with an HTTP endpoint that you host, instead of with an LLM judge. When a turn ends, the Weave agent scoring worker sends the turn to your endpoint in an HTTP `POST` and records the response as feedback on the turn. The result appears as a tag or rating on the **Signals** tab of the [Agents view](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/tracking/view-agent-signals.md).

This page covers remote scorers for agent turns. To score Calls traced with `@weave.op`, see [Score Calls with remote scorers](https://docs.coreweave.com/products/wandb/weave/guides/evaluation/remote-scorers.md). You configure remote scorers with the Python SDK or the Weave UI. The TypeScript SDK doesn't include `RemoteScorer`.
